exercises.name: Flat DB bench press
exercises.description: The main chest builder of the week. Two dumbbells pressed from a flat bench; loads the whole pec, front delts and triceps. Trainer: use your current flat-bench weight — set it once in Edit target, then try to beat it every session.
technique: Feet flat and planted, shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench.
Lower to the sides of the chest, elbows about 45° from your body — not flared to 90°.
Press up and slightly inward; stop just short of locking the elbows.
Control the descent, about two seconds down, no bouncing off the chest.

exercises.name: Seated DB overhead press
exercises.description: Seated shoulder press with dumbbells. Targets the front and side delts with the triceps assisting. Trainer: 2 kg below your usual overhead press weight, so the reps are clean.
technique: Back supported on the bench, feet planted, ribs down — don't arch to cheat.
Start with the dumbbells at ear height, palms forward.
Press straight up until the arms are nearly straight, dumbbells close together at the top.
Lower under control to ear height each rep; don't drop below that.

exercises.name: Squeeze press
exercises.description: Flat press with the two dumbbells pressed hard against each other the whole time. The constant inward squeeze keeps the inner chest under tension. Trainer: around 60% of your flat bench weight.
technique: Hold the dumbbells together, palms facing each other, and squeeze them into one another throughout.
Lower to the mid-chest, elbows tucked close to the ribs.
Press up while keeping the squeeze — if the dumbbells separate, the weight is too heavy.
Slow and deliberate; the squeeze matters more than the load.

exercises.name: DB lateral raise
exercises.description: Standing raise out to the sides. Isolates the side delts, which give the shoulders their width. Trainer: 8 kg.
technique: Slight bend in the elbows, torso leaning forward a touch, dumbbells at your sides.
Raise out to the sides until the arms are parallel to the floor, leading with the elbows.
Pinky slightly higher than the thumb at the top; don't shrug the traps up.
Lower slowly — no swinging or using the hips to start the rep.

exercises.name: Lying DB skullcrusher
exercises.description: Lying triceps extension with dumbbells. Lowers the weight towards the head and extends back up; works the long head of the triceps. Trainer: 8–10 kg per hand.
technique: Lie flat, arms straight above the chest, palms facing each other.
Keep the upper arms still and pointing slightly back over the head.
Bend only at the elbows, lowering the dumbbells beside the ears.
Extend back up without letting the elbows drift outward.

exercises.name: Pulley pushdown
exercises.description: Cable triceps pushdown with a bar or rope. Finishes the triceps with a controlled, constant-tension movement. Trainer: 17 kg on the stack.
technique: Stand tall, elbows pinned to your sides, slight forward lean.
Push down until the arms are fully straight and squeeze the triceps for a beat.
Let the handle rise only until the forearms pass parallel — the elbows stay put.
No leaning on the cable or driving with the shoulders.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raises
exercises.description: Hanging from a bar, bring the knees up towards the chest. Builds the lower abs and hip flexors while training grip.
technique: Hang with a full grip, shoulders slightly pulled down so you are not just dangling.
Tuck the pelvis and curl the knees up towards the chest — the lower back should round a little.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly without swinging.
If you swing, reset to a dead hang before the next rep.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.description: Static hold on one forearm with the body in a straight line. Trains the obliques and the muscles that stabilise the spine. Each set is one hold per side — log the seconds you held.
technique: Elbow directly under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered.
Lift the hips until shoulders, hips and ankles form a straight line.
Squeeze the glutes and keep the top hip from sinking or rotating back.
Breathe normally; stop the set when the line breaks, not when the clock says so.

exercises.name: Scapular pull-ups
exercises.description: Warm-up. Hanging from the bar with straight arms, pull the shoulder blades down and together to lift the body a few centimetres. Wakes up the lats and lower traps before the heavy pulling.
technique: Dead hang with straight arms and a full grip.
Without bending the elbows, drive the shoulders down and away from the ears.
Hold the top for a second, then let the shoulders rise back up slowly.
Small movement — the arms never bend.

exercises.name: Straight-arm pulldown (warm-up)
exercises.description: Light lat activation on the cable before the working sets. Not a working set — the goal is to feel the lats, not to fatigue them. Trainer: 10 kg on the stack.
technique: Stand facing the high pulley, slight hinge at the hips, arms straight.
Sweep the bar down to the thighs in an arc, keeping the elbows nearly locked.
Squeeze the lats at the bottom, then let the bar rise slowly overhead.
Keep the load light enough to feel the lats on every rep.

exercises.name: Kneeling single-arm pulley pulldown
exercises.description: Main lat exercise of the day. Kneeling under a high cable, pull one handle down to the hip. One arm at a time lets the lat go through its full range. Reps are per arm. Trainer: 15 kg on the stack.
technique: Kneel with the working arm reaching up towards the pulley, torso slightly rotated towards it.
Pull the elbow down and back towards your hip, keeping the shoulder down.
Squeeze the lat at the bottom for a beat.
Let the arm rise fully so the lat gets a stretch at the top of every rep.

exercises.name: Single-arm DB row
exercises.description: One-arm dumbbell row supported on a bench. Heavy lat and mid-back work with the free hand bracing. Reps are per side. Trainer: 22 kg.
technique: Hand and knee on the bench, back flat and parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down, shoulder blade relaxed.
Row the elbow up and back towards the hip, not straight up to the ceiling.
Lower all the way down for a stretch — no twisting the torso to lift it.

exercises.name: DB pullover
exercises.description: Lying across a bench, lower one dumbbell behind the head and pull it back over the chest. Stretches and loads the lats and serratus. Trainer: one 16 kg dumbbell.
technique: Lie on the bench, hold one dumbbell with both hands above the chest, slight elbow bend.
Lower it in an arc behind the head until you feel a stretch through the lats.
Keep the elbow bend the same throughout — this is not a triceps extension.
Pull back over to the chest by driving the upper arms, ribs kept down.

exercises.name: Face pulls
exercises.description: Rope pull to the face on a high cable. Rear delts, rotator cuff and mid traps — the shoulder-health exercise. Trainer: 15 kg on the stack.
technique: Rope at about forehead height, step back so the arms are extended.
Pull the rope towards the face with the elbows high and wide.
Finish with the hands beside the ears, as if showing off your biceps.
Light weight, full control — no leaning back to move the stack.

exercises.name: Incline DB curl
exercises.description: Curl performed seated on an incline bench with the arms hanging back. Puts the biceps long head under a stretch. Trainer: 10 kg per hand.
technique: Bench at about 45°, back and head on the pad, arms hanging straight down and slightly behind you.
Curl without moving the upper arm forward — elbows stay behind the torso.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
Don't shrug or swing; if you have to, the weight is too heavy.

exercises.name: Zottman curl
exercises.description: Curl up with the palms facing up, rotate at the top, lower with the palms facing down. Biceps on the way up, forearms and brachialis on the way down. Trainer: 8 kg per hand.
technique: Standing, curl the dumbbells with palms up as in a normal curl.
At the top, rotate the wrists so the palms face down.
Lower slowly with the palms down — this half is the point of the exercise.
Rotate back to palms up at the bottom and repeat.

exercises.name: Weighted crunch on bench
exercises.description: Crunch with a plate held on the chest, feet on a bench or knees bent. Adds load to the upper abs so they can progress like any other muscle. Trainer: 5–8 kg plate.
technique: Lie on your back, plate held against the chest, lower back pressed into the floor.
Curl the ribs towards the hips — the shoulder blades leave the floor, the lower back does not.
Exhale hard at the top and hold for a beat.
Lower slowly; don't pull on the neck or yank with the arms.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: Static front hold on the forearms. Trains the whole core to resist extension. Log the seconds held per set.
technique: Elbows under the shoulders, forearms flat, feet together or hip width.
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the pelvis so the lower back does not sag.
Push the floor away so the upper back is slightly rounded, not collapsed.
Hold a straight line from head to heels; stop the set when the hips drop.

exercises.name: Arnold press
exercises.description: Seated press that starts with the palms facing you and rotates to palms forward on the way up. Hits all three heads of the delts through the rotation. Trainer: 2 kg below your overhead press weight.
technique: Sit with back supported, dumbbells in front of the shoulders, palms facing you.
As you press, rotate the palms outward so they face forward at the top.
Keep the movement smooth — the rotation and the press happen together.
Reverse the rotation on the way down; don't let the elbows drop below the shoulders.

exercises.name: Incline DB press
exercises.description: Press on a bench set around 30°. Emphasises the upper chest and front delts. Trainer: 2 kg above the weight you used before.
technique: Bench at about 30°, shoulder blades pulled back and down, feet planted.
Lower the dumbbells to the upper chest with the elbows about 45° out.
Press up and slightly together, stopping just short of lockout.
Same controlled two-second descent as the flat press.

exercises.name: Close-grip DB press
exercises.description: Flat press with the dumbbells held close together and the elbows tucked in. Shifts the work towards the triceps and inner chest. Trainer: about 70–75% of your flat bench weight.
technique: Palms facing each other, dumbbells touching or nearly touching.
Lower with the elbows tucked close to the ribs, down to the lower chest.
Press up in a straight line, driving through the triceps.
Keep the wrists straight and the dumbbells close the whole rep.

exercises.name: DB upright row
exercises.description: Pull two dumbbells up the front of the body, leading with the elbows. Side delts and upper traps. Trainer: 10–12 kg per hand.
technique: Dumbbells hanging in front of the thighs, slightly wider than the hips.
Pull up with the elbows leading, hands staying below the elbows.
Stop when the elbows reach shoulder height — going higher pinches the shoulder.
Lower slowly; don't heave with the legs or lower back.

exercises.name: Prone incline Y-raise
exercises.description: Lying chest-down on an incline bench, raise light dumbbells up and out into a Y shape. Lower traps and rear delts, the small muscles that keep the shoulders healthy. Trainer: 2–3 kg per hand.
technique: Chest on the incline bench, arms hanging straight down, thumbs up.
Raise the arms up and out at about 45° so the body forms a Y at the top.
Lead with the thumbs and squeeze the shoulder blades down and together.
Very light weight; if the traps shrug up, go lighter.

exercises.name: Seated DB overhead extension
exercises.description: Seated, hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands and lower it behind the head. Loads the long head of the triceps in a stretched position. Trainer: one 16–18 kg dumbbell.
technique: Sit tall, both hands cupping the top plate of one dumbbell held overhead.
Lower it behind the head by bending only at the elbows; the upper arms stay by the ears.
Go as deep as the shoulders comfortably allow, then extend back to the top.
Keep the ribs down and don't flare the elbows out wide.

exercises.name: Kneeling pulley crunch
exercises.description: Kneeling under a high cable holding a rope at the head, crunch the ribs down towards the hips. Weighted upper-ab work with constant tension. Trainer: 15 kg on the stack.
technique: Kneel facing the stack, rope held at the sides of the head, hips staying still.
Crunch by rounding the spine and bringing the elbows towards the knees.
The hips don't move — if they hinge, you are using the hip flexors, not the abs.
Return slowly to a tall kneel with the abs stretched.

exercises.name: DB side bend
exercises.description: Standing with one dumbbell at the side, bend sideways and return. Loads the obliques. Reps are per side. Trainer: one 16 kg dumbbell.
technique: Stand tall, dumbbell in one hand, the other hand behind the head or on the hip.
Bend sideways towards the dumbbell, sliding it down the leg.
Return by pulling with the opposite oblique — don't lean forward or back.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.

exercises.name: Scapular pull-ups
exercises.description: Warm-up. Hanging from the bar with straight arms, pull the shoulder blades down and together to lift the body a few centimetres. Wakes up the lats and lower traps before the heavy pulling.
technique: Dead hang with straight arms and a full grip.
Without bending the elbows, drive the shoulders down and away from the ears.
Hold the top for a second, then let the shoulders rise back up slowly.
Small movement — the arms never bend.

exercises.name: Straight-arm pulldown (warm-up)
exercises.description: Light lat activation on the cable before the working sets. Not a working set — the goal is to feel the lats, not to fatigue them. Trainer: 10 kg on the stack.
technique: Stand facing the high pulley, slight hinge at the hips, arms straight.
Sweep the bar down to the thighs in an arc, keeping the elbows nearly locked.
Squeeze the lats at the bottom, then let the bar rise slowly overhead.
Keep the load light enough to feel the lats on every rep.

exercises.name: Chest-supported DB row, elbows flared
exercises.description: Main upper-back exercise of the day. Lying chest-down on an incline bench, row with the elbows out wide. Flaring the elbows shifts the work from the lats to the rear delts, rhomboids and mid traps. Trainer: 18 kg per hand.
technique: Chest stays glued to the bench the whole set — no lifting off to heave.
Row with the elbows out at about 60–90°, pulling towards the chest rather than the hips.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together hard at the top.
Lower all the way until the shoulder blades spread apart.

exercises.name: Straight-arm pulldown
exercises.description: The working version of the cable straight-arm pulldown. Isolates the lats without the biceps helping. Trainer: 17 kg on the stack.
technique: Slight hinge at the hips, arms straight with a soft elbow, chest up.
Sweep the bar down in an arc to the thighs, driving with the lats.
Squeeze at the bottom for a beat.
Let the bar rise slowly until the arms are overhead and the lats are stretched.

exercises.name: Prone incline T-raise
exercises.description: Chest-down on an incline bench, raise light dumbbells straight out to the sides into a T. Rear delts and mid traps. Trainer: 2–3 kg per hand.
technique: Chest on the bench, arms hanging straight down, palms facing forward or thumbs up.
Raise the arms straight out to the sides to shoulder height.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower slowly; keep the neck relaxed and the traps from shrugging.

exercises.name: DB shrugs
exercises.description: Standing with heavy dumbbells at the sides, shrug the shoulders straight up. Upper traps. Trainer: 24–28 kg per hand.
technique: Stand tall, dumbbells at the sides, arms straight and relaxed.
Shrug the shoulders straight up towards the ears — not rolled forward or back.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly to a full stretch; don't bend the elbows to help.

exercises.name: Hammer curl
exercises.description: Curl with the palms facing each other throughout. Hits the brachialis and forearms as well as the biceps — adds arm thickness. Trainer: 12 kg per hand.
technique: Stand tall, dumbbells at the sides, palms facing the thighs.
Curl up keeping the thumb on top the whole way.
Elbows stay by the ribs; don't swing them forward.
Lower under control to a full extension.

exercises.name: Spider curl
exercises.description: Curl performed chest-down on an incline bench with the arms hanging in front. The opposite of the incline curl — the biceps work in a shortened position, giving a hard peak contraction. Trainer: 8 kg per hand.
technique: Chest on the incline bench, arms hanging straight down in front, palms forward.
Curl up without letting the upper arms swing back.
Squeeze hard at the top — this is the whole point of the exercise.
Lower slowly to a full stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Hanging leg raises
exercises.description: The straight-leg version of the knee raise. Hanging from a bar, lift the legs to horizontal or higher. Harder on the lower abs and hip flexors.
technique: Hang with a full grip, shoulders slightly pulled down.
Tuck the pelvis first, then raise the straight legs to at least parallel.
Pause at the top and lower slowly without swinging.
If the legs must bend, bend them the same amount every rep.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.description: Static hold on one forearm with the body in a straight line. Trains the obliques and the muscles that stabilise the spine. Each set is one hold per side — log the seconds you held.
technique: Elbow directly under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered.
Lift the hips until shoulders, hips and ankles form a straight line.
Squeeze the glutes and keep the top hip from sinking or rotating back.
Breathe normally; stop the set when the line breaks, not when the clock says so.
